objective_of_lab: I was trying to learn how basic C programming constructs work in practical programs, including input and output, arithmetic operations, conditions, switch statements, comparison, and the use of variables. I also wanted to understand how different inputs affect the result of a program.

P1.problem_understanding: The problem was to determine whether an entered integer is even or odd.
P1.logic_approach: Read the integer and used the remainder after division by 2. If the remainder was zero I treated it as even; otherwise it was odd. The condition selected the final message.
P1.what_i_observed: I noticed that numbers divisible by 2 are classified as even, while numbers with a remainder of 1 are classified as odd.

P2.problem_understanding: The problem was to classify an integer as positive, negative, or zero.
P2.logic_approach: Compared the input with zero. The first condition checked whether it was greater than zero, another checked whether it was less than zero, and otherwise it was zero.
P2.what_i_observed: I observed that zero needs its own case because it is neither positive nor negative.

P3.problem_understanding: The problem was to identify whether an input character is uppercase, lowercase, a digit, or a special character.
P3.logic_approach: Compared the character against the ranges for uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and digits. If it did not match any of these categories, I treated it as a special character.
P3.what_i_observed: I observed that a character can be classified into different categories by checking its ASCII range.

P4.problem_understanding: The problem was to determine whether a given year is a leap year.
P4.logic_approach: Checked divisibility by 400, and otherwise checked the divisibility conditions involving 4 and 100. The combined conditions determined the result.
P4.what_i_observed: I noticed that a year divisible by 100 is not normally a leap year unless it is also divisible by 400.

P5.problem_understanding: The problem was to find how much memory common C data types occupy.
P5.logic_approach: Used sizeof with different data types and printed the returned sizes.

important_variables.purpose: stores a size returned by sizeof

P5.what_i_observed: I observed that the size of a data type can depend on the compiler and system.

P6.problem_understanding: The problem was to perform an arithmetic operation selected from a menu.
P6.logic_approach: Read two numbers and a menu choice. A switch statement selected addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, modulus, or power.

P7.problem_understanding: The problem was to exchange two integer values without using a third temporary variable.
P7.logic_approach: Changed the values using arithmetic operations so that the original values were exchanged.

important_variables.purpose: hold the two values being exchanged

P7.what_i_observed: I noticed that the values can be exchanged without declaring a separate temporary variable.

P8.problem_understanding: The problem was to exchange two values using a temporary variable.
P8.logic_approach: Stored the first value in a temporary variable, moved the second value into the first variable, and then restored the saved value into the second variable.

P9.problem_understanding: The problem was to determine whether a positive integer is a perfect square without using sqrt.
P9.logic_approach: Repeatedly increased a candidate value and compared its square with the input. The process stopped when the square reached or exceeded the input.
P9.what_i_observed: I observed that the loop tests possible square roots one by one.

P10.problem_understanding: The problem was to assign a grade according to a student's marks.
P10.logic_approach: Compared the marks against grade ranges using if-else conditions. The first matching range determined the grade.
P10.what_i_observed: I noticed that the order of the conditions matters because the first matching range is selected.

P11.problem_understanding: The problem was to create a calculator menu that also handles invalid choices and division by zero.
P11.logic_approach: Used a switch statement to select the requested operation and added a default case for an invalid choice. Before division I checked whether the divisor was zero.
P11.what_i_observed: I noticed that division by zero must be handled separately to avoid an invalid calculation.

P12.problem_understanding: The problem was to find the largest among three numbers.
P12.logic_approach: Used conditional expressions to compare the values and retain the largest one.
P12.what_i_observed: I observed that the ternary operator can express a simple conditional selection compactly.

P13.problem_understanding: The problem was to convert a grade point into a corresponding letter grade.
P13.logic_approach: Used a switch-based mapping to associate the supplied grade point with its letter grade.
P13.what_i_observed: I observed that a switch statement is useful when several discrete values map to predefined results.
